valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 17 Nov 2026. (1) Business: one business in effect, cables and conductors (cables 81% of 2025/26 segment profit before finance and other income; PVC compound 10% and aluminium/copper rods and accessories 7% mostly feed the cable plants: Annual Report 2025/26, p. 183). So one sector beta. (2) Damodaran's emerging-markets dataset (betaEmerg) could NOT be opened: his site is blocked by this run's network settings. Stand-in from a web-search extract of his global table (January 2026): Electrical Equipment, 1,158 firms, levered 1.37, D/E 13.74%, unlevered 1.25, cash 7.08% of firm value, unlevered corrected for cash 1.34. (3) Net cash (Rs 10.4bn at 30 Sep 2026, about 14% of market value), so debt to equity 0 and no relevering, as for other net-cash companies on this site: 1.34. Weighting the cash pile at a beta of zero would give an equity beta of about 1.15 (1.34 × 62/73), so 1.34 is on the cautious side. (4) Local 5-year betas: none found (GuruFocus shows none; no vendor figure in search results). (5) Higher of 1.34 and (no local figure) = 1.34. (6) Within 0.3–2, but high for a CSE share: the global sector includes many technology-heavy equipment makers; ACL's profit does swing with copper (−49% in 2023/24). (7) Into the formula by scripts/reinvestment.py. Provisional: refresh in January 2027 with Damodaran's emerging-markets file and local 5-year betas.

valuationInputs.name: Cost of equity
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (17 Nov 2026): 8.24% + 1.34 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 22.0%, ±1.5 points. Replaces the hand-set 18% / 16.5% / 15% of 11 Nov, as the analysis brief now requires the shared CAPM method.

valuationInputs.name: WACC
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (17 Nov 2026): net cash Rs 10.37bn (Sep 2026), so debt weight 0% and WACC = cost of equity. Cost of debt 7.11% (interest paid 0.128 ÷ average borrowings and leases 1.80, FY 2026; short-term AWPLR-linked loans, below the calculator's usual range but irrelevant at 0% weight).

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 4% / 8% / 11%; supported 23.9% (reinvestment rate 68.8% × return on capital 34.7%, FY 2026). All within 2 pts.
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py on the FY 2026 figures. The supported rate is flattered: Rs 4.34bn of the Rs 4.37bn reinvestment was stock and receivables built up as copper prices rose (price, not volume). Profit kept × ROE gives 17.6%.

valuationInputs.name: Growth
valuationInputs.value: Bear 4% then 4% / Base 8% then 5% / Bull 11% then 6%
valuationInputs.reason: Five years, then long-run, below the 12.24% bond and WACC; long-run reinvestment 33% / 31% / 30% of after-tax operating profit. Revenue grew 21% in FY 2026 and 22% in H1 FY2027, mostly copper prices and exports.

valuationInputs.name: Return on new capital
valuationInputs.reason: Trailing after-tax operating profit Rs 5.9bn over operating capital about Rs 31.8bn at Sep 2026 (total equity 46.39 − net cash 10.37 − investment property, associates and FVOCI shares 4.24) = 18.5%; the calculator's 34.7% uses owners' equity only and the March 2025 base.

valuationInputs.name: Cash after maintenance capex (start)
valuationInputs.value: Bear Rs 4.8bn / Base Rs 5.9bn / Bull Rs 6.4bn
valuationInputs.reason: After-tax operating profit (maintenance capex ≈ depreciation, calculator range Rs 0.368 / 0.368 / 0.354bn). Not the calculator's FY 2026 cash figure (Rs 1.16bn), which is after Rs 4.34bn of working capital build that the DCF already charges as reinvestment.

valuationInputs.name: After-tax operating profit (start)
valuationInputs.value: Bear Rs 4.8bn / Base Rs 5.9bn / Bull Rs 6.4bn
valuationInputs.reason: Trailing operating profit Rs 9.20bn less the one-off Rs 0.70bn investment property gain = Rs 8.50bn × (1 − 30.8%) = Rs 5.88bn. Bear about the FY 2025 level (copper falls).

valuationInputs.name: Maintenance capex basis
valuationInputs.reason: No company split. Capex booked Rs 0.40bn vs depreciation Rs 0.37bn in FY 2026; no growth project named, no capital commitments.

valuationInputs.name: Owners' share and other assets
valuationInputs.reason: Minorities 14.1% of total equity at Sep 2026 (6.53 of 46.39), 13–15% of profit. Investment property 2.53 + associates 0.85 + FVOCI shares 0.86 at book, added to the DCF.

valuationInputs.name: Long-run ROE
valuationInputs.reason: Five-year average about 21%, including a 29% year (2022/23); 11% in 2023/24; 18.7% FY 2026.

valuationInputs.name: Long-term growth
valuationInputs.reason: Now the same in every method (DCF, P/B, P/E, residual income); 6% / 6.5% / 7% before. Below the 12.24% bond yield.

valuationInputs.name: EPS to March 2027 × P/E
valuationInputs.reason: H1 EPS Rs 4.61; H2 Rs 2.99 / 4.49 / 5.69 (last year 4.52). Base equals the Rs 9.13 run-rate. P/E justified at the cost of equity: payout (1 − g ÷ ROE) ÷ (cost of equity − g). Before: 7.00 × 6 / 9.00 × 8 / 10.50 × 10.

valuationInputs.name: Residual income start ROE
valuationInputs.reason: Twelve-month ROE about 18%. Payout 8% for five years.

valuationInputs.name: Methods used
valuationInputs.value: Whole-company DCF, P/E, justified P/B, residual income
valuationInputs.reason: DCF added (brief now requires it); it starts from operating profit rather than one year's cash flow because copper stock swings cash flow. Dividend model left out (payout about 7%).

openQuestions: Q3 results (to December 2026, due by mid-February): does the gross margin recover from 24% (26–28% a year earlier), and does EPS keep pace with the base case's second half of Rs 4.49?
Does inventory (Rs 19.1bn) start to fall and release cash, and are the Rs 4.4bn of short-term loans repaid?
Exchange gains and losses: a Rs 590mn gain in Q1 then a Rs 144mn loss in Q2; how big is the swing next quarter?
Beta: in January 2027 replace the web-search stand-in (global Electrical Equipment 1.34) with Damodaran's emerging-markets figure, and look for three local 5-year betas.
Bond yield and default spread: if the 10-year yield moves more than 1 point, refresh market inputs (a lower required return lifts fair value the most).
Exports (Rs 6.23bn in six months, up 46%): can the growth continue?
Copper price direction and its effect on stock values (not covered in the reports).

changeLog.summary: Requested from Telegram (/update ACL.N0000 COCO.N0000 DIST.N0000 HAYL.N0000 JINS.N0000 RHL.N0000). Updated from the interim report to 30 September 2026. Quarter flat: revenue up 26% to Rs 14.30bn, gross margin 23.8% (26.5%), Rs 144mn exchange loss, EPS Rs 2.04 (Rs 2.06); six months EPS Rs 4.61 (Rs 4.30). NAV Rs 55.46 (Rs 54.04 in June). Inventory Rs 19.08bn, operating cash flow minus Rs 4.66bn for the half, short-term loans Rs 4.43bn, net cash about Rs 10.4bn. Dividend Rs 0.60 for 2025/26 paid 26 Oct 2026. No valuation inputs changed; no restatements found. Fair value Rs 63.50 → 64.70 only from the higher NAV (P/B and residual income). Fair value Rs 64.70, buy Rs 55.00, strong buy Rs 48.50; price Rs 101.50 (CSE close 13 Nov 2026). Business tests 3 of 4 (fails cash), category 2 watch list, unchanged. Note: the 11 Nov residual-income bull case used a starting ROE of 19% (18% in bear and base); kept and now stated. Copper prices not in the report, so not assessed.

changeLog.basedOn: H1 FY2027 (to Sep 2026), with the FY 2026 annual report re-read in full
changeLog.summary: Requested from Telegram (/redo ACL.N0000 full). Rebuilt the record and analysis from the CSE copies of the 2025/26 annual report and the September 2026 interim. Added the reinvestment figures for FY 2025 and FY 2026 (capex booked 0.31 / 0.40, depreciation 0.36 / 0.37, working capital build 1.50 / 4.34, operating profit 7.47 / 9.18 incl. a 0.70bn investment property gain, tax 32.1% / 30.8%, interest paid in operating cash 0.27 / 0.13, borrowings 1.39 / 2.18, net cash 12.5 / 14.8, minorities), a Q2 FY2027 quarter and a 12-month EPS of Rs 9.13. Corrected the cash flow page reference (p. 125, not p. 124). No restatements found. Applied the current brief: beta 1.34 (provisional, Damodaran global Electrical Equipment via web search; his site and local 5-year betas unavailable), cost of equity = WACC 22.0% (16.5% before), whole-company DCF added, P/E multiples now justified at the cost of equity, long-term growth 4/5/6% in every method, growth check and run-rate checks pass. Fair value Rs 64.70 → 39.10, buy Rs 55.00 → 33.20, strong buy Rs 48.50 → 29.30; price Rs 101.00 (CSE close 17 Nov 2026). Business tests 3 of 4 (fails cash), category 2 watch list, unchanged. The fall is driven by the required return; at a cash-weighted beta of 1.15 fair value would be about Rs 44.50.
